Hon'ble Shri Justice Narendra Kumar Vyas Order on Board 13/08/2024
1.

This is the first bail application filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of regular bail to the applicant, who has been arrested on 14.03.2024 in connection with Crime No. 102/2024, registered at Police Station- Torwa, District- Bilaspur (C.G.) for the offence punishable under Sections 376 of I.P.C. & Section 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
2. Case of the prosecution in brief is that father of the victim lodged a complaint before the police station alleging that on 01.12.2024 the applicant along with other persons took the minor victim N. Ravikant Kurmi vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132755154/
1 with him and committed rape with her.

entities.text: N. Ravikant Kurmi vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
On the basis of the complaint lodged by father of the victim,
the offence as aforestated has been registered against the applicant.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the crime in question.
He would further submit that the victim was not minor on the date of incident, therefore, the offence under the POCSO Act is not made out.
He would further submit that there was love affair between the applicant and the victim and a concocted FIR has lodged against the applicant.

He would further submit that as per the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. as well as in the court statement, she has not supported case of the prosecution as she denied commission of offence by the applicant.

He would further submit that the applicant is in jail since 14.03.2024, the trial is likely to take some time for its final disposal,
therefore, the applicant may be enlarged on bail.
4.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes the bail application and would submit that there is sufficient material available in the case diary against the applicant regarding commission of offence.

She would further submit that the victim is aged below 18 years, therefore,
therefore, the offence under the POCSO Act is made out against the applicant.
She would further submit that the certificate place on record clearly shows that the victim was minor on the date of incident.
Hence, the application for grant of bail may be rejected.

5. In pursuance of direction issued by this Court, the victim was appeared before this Court through concerned DLSA on 22.07.2024 and submitted that she has no objection in granting bail to the applicant.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

7. Considering the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. as well as the court statement wherein she denied commission of offence by the applicant and also considering that the applicant is in jail since 14.03.2024 and the conclusion of the trial may take some time,
without commenting anything on merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a fit case to grant bail to the applicant.
8. Accordingly, the bail application filed under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs. 25,000/-
with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial court.
He shall appear before the trial court on each and every date given by the said trial court, till disposal of the trial.
Certified copy as per rules.
